sentences.text: Learned Senior Advocate appearing for the applicants submitted that impugned orders are against facts and law and thus, liable to be set aside.

The trial of the case in question is not being conducted in accordance with law and that no proper opportunity is being provided to the counsel for the applicants-accused for cross-examination of the witnesses and to submit the necessary documents as per law.
It was submitted that the impugned orders are perverse and against law and thus, the same are not sustainable.
Learned senior Advocate has raised mainly following points:

(i) Learned Senior counsel submitted that the learned Trial Court refused to mark the pen drive containing the video of a press conference held by P.W.-11 Mohd. Shafiq,
on the ground that P.W.-11 has admitted the contents of the video, which is against the law.
Further, the trial court has directed the defence for not to cross-examine the P.W.11 (Mohd Shafiq) to show his collusion with the informant.
There is no rule of law, which prohibits defence to show that prosecution witness has deposed falsely or he has colluded with the first informant.

The trial court has rejected the application of defence for production of video pertaining to the filing of nomination papers,
which was an important evidence for confrontation and cross-examination of P.W.10 Gajender Singh.
(ii) It was submitted that the trial court has erroneously allowed the prosecution to copy the statements, recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., from the case diary, in examination in chief of the investigating officer Narender Tyagi (P.W.14), which was in-admissible evidence and contrary to the provisions of Section 162 Cr.P.C..

The trial court has allowed exhibiting of the photocopy of EOT/MLR Register of Queens Mary Hospital, Lucknow in examination-in-chief of P.W.14 Narender Tyagi, without production of Dr. Uma Singh, Queen Mary Hospital.

(iii) It is next submitted that a pure civil exercise of correction of the date of birth of applicant No.2 in Government record was given criminal colour by local B.J.P. leader Akash Saxena, who lodged first information report of case vide crime no. 4/2019,
alleging forgery in record pertaining to birth certificate of applicant No-2.

(iv) It was pointed that the accused persons have moved discharge applications on 10.03.2021 with stand that no case of criminal conspiracy is made out and the charge sheet was not submitted under section 120-B IPC.

Thereafter on 03.08.2021 matter was heard on merits but prosecution sought time to respond to the merits of the defence of accused persons and on 05.08.2021 the prosecution was granted time to file compilation of case laws.

On 11.08.2021 the prosecution has sought more time for filing of case laws but on the same day in complete disregard to the provisions of law,
an application supported with an affidavit was filed by the complainant along with supplementary charge-sheet dated 10.08.2021 under section 120B IPC before the trial court.

The applicants have filed detailed objections to the said supplementary charge-sheet but the discharge application and objections of the accused persons were rejected by the trial court in an arbitrary manner.

sentences.text: Learned Senior Advocate submitted that the Public Prosecutor has openly asked leading questions, which was objected to in terms of two applications dated 31.08.2021 and the said applications were decided on the same day by short hand written order by the trial court but later on a typed order was passed and the hand written order dated 31.08.2021 was struck out.

(vi) It is next submitted that on 02.09.2021 the applicants have filed an application No.67B dated 02.09.2021 seeking the video recording of the trial proceedings to show that prosecution was tutoring P.W.1 and even offering clarificatory answers in open court during proceedings but that application was not decided by the trial court till 20.09.2021 and the statement of P.W.1 Aakash Saxena was completed on 04.09.2021 by closing the deposition of P.W.1 in an arbitrary manner.
On the same day two applications were filed by the applicants for summoning of records pertaining the complaints given by the complainant but the same were rejected by the Trial Court.

(vii) It is further submitted that after cross-examination of P.W.-6 Head Clerk Rai Singh, the prosecution has filed an application under Section 311 Cr.P.C. to summon Sri Gajendra Singh, the then returning officer, who was neither examined during investigation nor cited as witness in the charge-sheet but despite that he was summoned and examined as witness (PW-10).
(viii) It is further submitted that one application was filed by the applicants seeking production of video of proceedings of filing of nomination papers before PW-10 but it was rejected.
On 31.10.2022 one application was filed on behalf of applicants for production of register maintained by the returning officer and the same was disposed of by the trial court by refusing the prayer.

On 17.11.2022 the prosecution has filed an application under Section 311 Cr.P.C. for summoning three persons, namely,
Hameed, Mohd. Shafiq and Dinesh Goyal, who were neither examined during investigation nor cited as witness in charge-sheet, but that application was allowed.
On 07.12.2022 an application was filed by the applicants seeking permission to cross-examine P.W-11 Mohd Shafiq on certain facts but it was rejected in an arbitrary manner.
On 14.12.2022 an application seeking adjournment on behalf of applicants for short accommodation, was rejected by the trial court.
On 15.12.2022 another application seeking adjournment on just ground was allowed by imposing heavy costs of Rs.5,000/-.

(ix) Learned Senior counsel has referred certain other facts, as mentioned in the supporting affidavit, and submitted that applications moved on behalf of applicants on just and proper grounds are being rejected by the trial court in an arbitrary manner and that no proper opportunity is being granted to the accused-applicants during trial to defend themselves.

Referring to the facts of the matter, it was submitted that the impugned orders are liable to be set aside and that a case for allowing the prayers as mentioned in the prayer clause of application under Section Mohammad Azam Khan And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8607718/
4 482 Cr.P.C., is made out.
4. Per contra, learned Additional Advocate General as well as learned counsel for the complainant have opposed the application and submitted that there is no material illegality or perversity in the impugned orders and that the trial of the case is being conducted in accordance with law and proper opportunity is being granted to the defence as per provisions of law.

sentences.text: Merely because certain applications filed by the applicants have been rejected by the trial court, it cannot be said that trial is not being conducted in accordance with law.
If the applicants are aggrieved by any order of the trial court, they have opportunity to challenge the same in higher courts in accordance with law.
Referring to the facts of the matter, it was submitted that there is no illegality or perversity in the impugned orders.
It was submitted that some minor procedural issues are being raised by the applicants/accused with intention to delay the proceedings of trial.
It was submitted that this application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has no substance and thus, liable to be dismissed.
5. I have considered rival submissions and perused the record.
6. At the outset it may be noticed that the applicants have raised several issues pertaining to different stages of trial in this one petition.
Before proceeding further it would be pertinent to mention that an accused has innate right to be treated fairly in criminal prosecution.
Fair, just and reasonable procedure trial is implicit in Article 21 of the Constitution.
Denial of a fair trial is an injustice to both the accused and the victim.

Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Himanshu Singh Sabharwal vs. State of M.P. (Transfer Petition (crl.) 175 of 2007), decided on 12.03.2008, observed as under:
"6.

entities.text: Himanshu Singh Sabharwal vs. State of M.P. (Transfer Petition (crl.) 175 of 2007)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The principle of fair trial now informs and energises many areas of the law.
It is reflected in numerous rules and practices.

It is a constant, ongoing development process continually adapted to new and changing circumstances, and exigencies of the situation - peculiar at times and related to the nature of crime, persons involved - directly or operating behind, social impact and societal needs and even so many powerful balancing factors which may come in the way of administration of criminal justice system.
7.xxxxxxxxxxxxx 8.

This Court has often emphasised that in a criminal case the fate of the proceedings cannot always be left entirely in the hands of the parties, crimes being public wrongs in breach and violation of public rights and duties, which affect the whole community as a community and harmful to the society in general.
The concept of fair trial entails familiar triangulation of interests of the accused, the victim and the society and it is the community that acts through the State and prosecuting agencies.
Interests of society is not to be treated completely with disdain and as persona non grata.

Courts have always been considered to have an over-riding duty to maintain public confidence in the administration of justice - often referred to as the duty to vindicate and uphold the 'majesty of the law'.

Due administration of justice has always been Mohammad Azam Khan And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8607718/
5 viewed as a continuous process, not confined to determination of the particular case,
protecting its ability to function as a Court of law in the future as in the case before it.

entities.text: Mohammad Azam Khan And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If a criminal Court is to be an effective instrument in dispensing justice, the Presiding Judge must cease to be a spectator and a mere recording machine by becoming a participant in the trial evincing intelligence, active interest and elicit all relevant materials necessary for reaching the correct conclusion, to find out the truth, and administer justice with fairness and impartiality both to the parties and to the community it serves.

Courts administering criminal justice cannot turn a blind eye to vexatious or oppressive conduct that has occurred in relation to proceedings, even if a fair trial is still possible, except at the risk of undermining the fair name and standing of the judges as impartial and independent adjudicators.
9. The principles of rule of law and due process are closely linked with human rights protection.
Such rights can be protected effectively when a citizen has recourse to the Courts of law.
It has to be unmistakably understood that a trial which is primarily aimed at ascertaining truth has to be fair to all concerned.

There can be no analytical,
all comprehensive or exhaustive definition of the concept of a fair trial, and it may have to be determined in seemingly infinite variety of actual situations with the ultimate object in mind viz. whether something that was done or said either before or at the trial deprived the quality of fairness to a degree where a miscarriage of justice has resulted.
It will not be correct to say that it is only the accused who must be fairly dealt with.
That would be turning Nelson's eyes to the needs of the society at large and the victims or their family members and relatives.
Each one has an inbuilt right to be dealt with fairly in a criminal trial.
Denial of a fair trial is as much injustice to the accused as is to the victim and the society.
Fair trial obviously would mean a trial before an impartial Judge, a fair prosecutor and atmosphere of judicial calm.

Fair trial means a trial in which bias or prejudice for or against the accused, the witnesses,
or the cause which is being tried is eliminated.
If the witnesses get threatened or are forced to give false evidence that also would not result in a fair trial.

The failure to hear material witnesses is certainly denial of fair trial.''
7.
It was further observed that failure to accord fair hearing either to the accused or the prosecution violates even minimum standards of due process of law.

It is inherent in the concept of due process of law, that condemnation should be rendered only after the trial in which the hearing is a real one,
not sham or a mere farce and pretence.
Since the fair hearing requires an opportunity to preserve the process, it may be vitiated and violated by an overhasty stage-managed, tailored and partisan trial.

The fair trial for a criminal offence consists not only in technical observance of the frame and forms of law, but also in recognition and just application of its principles in substance, to find out the truth and prevent miscarriage of justice.

8. It has also to be kept in view that section 482 of CrPC confers inherent powers upon the Court to make orders necessary to prevent the abuse of the process of the court or to secure the ends of justice.
Normally the High Court would not use its inherent authority to halt legal action, annul just orders or to interfere in an ongoing trial.

Such powers have to be exercise when doing so furthers the Mohammad Azam Khan And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8607718/
6 interests of justice.

sentences.text:
The court has to ensure that its involvement does not infringe upon the parties'
rights or transgress the norms of natural justice.
The inherent powers of the court under Section 482 CrPC have to be exercised in extraordinary situations.

9. Coming to the facts of the instant case, it may be observed that so far the grievance of the applicants regarding impugned order dated 07.12.2022 is concerned, whereby, the application of the applicants-accused to mark the pen-drive produced during cross-examination of P.W-11 (Mohd Shafiq) has been refused, it may be stated that it is settled practice in criminal trials that if during cross-examination of a witness, the defence/accused confronts the witness with some relevant document, such document may be taken on record by putting a mark number on such document but it is for the trial court to consider whether the such document is having relevancy in the trial or not.
If any irrelevant document is produced by the defence during cross-examination of a witness, the court may decline to take such document on record.

In the instant matter, it appears that a pen-drive was produced before the trial court during cross-examination of PW-11 (Mohd Shafiq),
which allegedly pertains to a press conference held by PW-11 (Mohd Shafiq), along with one Azaz Ahmad, in support of Aakash Saxena (informant of the case), who was candidate of B.J.P. for bye-election.

Here, it would be pertinent to mention that the essence of the prosecution case is regarding alleged falseness of date of birth of applicant No.2 Mohammad Abdullah Azam Khan and forgery in some documents pertaining to date of birth of said accused and use of forged documents.
It appears that the contents of the said pen drive / CD were admitted by PW-11 (Mohd Shafiq).
Further, the pen-drive falls within the ambit of electronic record and such document has to be considered in view of provisions of Section 65A and 65B of Evidence Act.
Here, it would be relevant to mention that the defence has opportunity to produce relevant documentary evidence at the stage of defence evidence.

In view of attending facts and circumstances of the matter, it cannot be said by declining to take the said pen drive / CD on record, the trial court committed any such patent illegality or perversity so as to require any interference by this court, particularly when the defence has opportunity to led defence evidence at the appropriate stage.

Thus, the impugned order dated 07.12.2022, whereby, the application of the applicants-accused to mark the pen-drive produced during cross-examination of P.W-11 (Mohd Shafiq) has been declined, calls no interference.

10. So far as the prayer of the applicants mentioned in clause (B) is concerned, by the impugned order dated 7.12.2022 the trial court has overruled some questions and permitted some questions to be asked and directed that no further question, to prove the alleged collusion of the witness with the first informant, shall be asked.

No doubt the trial court has power to overrule a question, being asked in cross-examination of a witness, but such discretion has to be exercised in accordance with law keeping in view the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case.

It appears that defence has filed an application before the Trial Court alleging that PW-11 (Mohd Shafiq) has collusion with first informant and the permission was sought to ask certain questions from P.W.-11 (Mohd Shafiq) in cross-examination to indicate the alleged collusion between the two.
It can not be said that the said aspect of alleged collusion is irrelevant for proceedings in trial.
The right of cross-examination of a witness is a powerful and effective instrument in the hand of accused for bringing out and testing the truth of the evidence of witness.

Cross-examination is not a mere forum of procedure but is a matter of substance and accused has a right to put its version in the cross-examination to assail the correctness of the statement of the witness as right to cross-examination is a valuable right.

7 146 of the Indian Evidence Act permits the accused to ask questions to the witness to test his veracity, to discover his position in life and to shake his credit, by injuring his character.

sentences.text:
However,
provisions of section 149, 150 and 151 of Evidence Act provide certain contingencies like when question not to be asked without reasonable grounds and power of the Court to forbid any indecent and scandalous question.

It is settled law that when allegations/accusations are made against any person facing trial, that party should have ample opportunity to cross-examine the person who had given the evidence against him.
It is only after such an opportunity is given and the witness is cross-examined, the evidence becomes admissible.

Having taken into consideration the facts of the instant matter, it appears that the direction of the trial court vide impugned order that no more question shall be asked by the defence regarding alleged collusion of P.W.-11 (Mohd Shafiq) with the first informant, is not in accordance with law and regarding this point interference is warranted by this court.
11.

Regarding the prayer mentioned in clause (C), it appears that an application was filed on behalf of applicants-accused under Section 91 Cr.P.C. for production of video recording of entire proceedings of filing of nomination papers by the candidates on 27.01.2017 for election of legislative assembly pertaining to Saur Constituency.
This application was rejected by the Trial Court vide impugned order dated 31.10.2022.

Section 91 Cr.P.C. provides that whenever the court considers that production of any document or any other thing is necessary or desirable for the purpose of investigation/enquiry or trial or for other proceedings before the court, such court may summon such documents or thing.
In the instant matter as stated above, the essence of prosecution case revolves around the falseness/forgery in some documents regarding date of birth of applicant No.2.
The trial court has considered the matter and found the said material/ video recording irrelevant.
In view of the attending facts and circumstances of the matter, it cannot be said that the impugned order dated 31.10.2022 is suffering from any material illegality or perversity.
12. So far the prayer mentioned in clause (D) in application under section 482 Cr.P.C. is concerned

,
it may be mentioned that no such direction, as sought by the applicants-accused, can be issued by this Court, as the trial of the case is going on.

This court cannot make any such declaration that statements of witnesses Dr. Uma Singh, Sudhir Kumar and Tejpal Verma were copied down in examination-in-chief from case diary or that the said statements are not admissible or that the same shall not be read in evidence.
The issuance of such direction would be against all norms of law.
The prayer sought by the applicants is wholly misconceived.
However, the applicants may raise their objections at time of final hearing and it is for the trial court to consider and decide whether the alleged evidence is admissible or not.

13. Similarly, the directions sought by the applicants vide prayer clause (E) of the application, can not be allowed and no such direction can be issued by this Court that the documents exhibits Ka-64,
Ka-65, Ka-366, Ka-67 and Ka-68 are not proved or the same shall not be read in evidence.
The defence would have liberty to raise its grievances/objections at the time of final argument.

While the trial is going on before the trial court, this court cannot issue any such direction, in as much-as, this court cannot express any opinion regarding admissibility or reliability of any evidence at this stage.
It is for the trial court to consider and decide the same at appropriate stage in accordance with law.

sentences.text: After considering all relevant facts and material on record, it appears that except the prayer made in clause (B) of the application under section 482 CrPC, no other interference is called in exercise of powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
Thus, the prayers sought by the applicants-accused vide clause (A), (C), (D) and (E) in the application under section 482 Cr.P.C. are hereby refused.

15. So far the prayer mentioned in clause (B) of the application is concerned, the direction of trial court vide impugned order dated 07.12.2022 that no more question shall be asked by the defence regarding alleged collusion of P.W.-11 (Mohd Shafiq) with the first informant
, is set aside and the trial court is directed that the defence would be provided a reasonable opportunity to cross-examine P.W.-11 (Mohd Shafiq) regarding alleged collusion of PW-11 with informant.

However, if any question is found not relevant or asked without any reasonable ground or falls in any category prohibited by law, the trial court may forbid or disallow such question in accordance with law.

It is further directed that in case, the statement of P.W.-11 has already been completed and closed, the defence would be at liberty to file an application under Section 311 Cr.P.C for recalling of said witness (PW -11) and in case such an application is filed within a period of two weeks from today,
the same shall be considered and decided by the trial court expeditiously in accordance with law and keeping in view of observations made in this order.

16. Before parting with this order, it may be observed that while the trial of the case is going on, this court can not issue any such direction that a document or evidence is admissible or not admissible.
This court can not even express any opinion on merits of the case lest it may prejudice the case of either party.
Needless to state that the trial court shall ensure that the trial is conducted in a free and fair manner in accordance with law.
17. With aforesaid observations, the application is disposed of.

It is further directed that in case, the statement of P.W.-11 has already been completed and closed, the defence would be at liberty to file an application under Section 311 Cr.P.C for recalling of said witness (PW -11) and in case such an application is filed within a period of two weeks from today,
the same shall be considered and decided by the trial court expeditiously in accordance with law and keeping in view of observations made in this order.
